subject: Guaranteed lanes + consumption discount inquiry
messages:
From: Danielle Harper <d.harper@gridly.com>
To: Chloe Martin <chloe.martin@redwood.ai>
Date: Sun, 17 May 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: SLA/packaging question — guaranteed lane during peaks

Hi Chloe,

Thanks for the quick intro last week. A few follow-ups from our platform team as we scope the pilot:

- We need a guaranteed lane (dedicated routing/priority) during our morning peak window (09:00–11:00 PT) that can sustain ~500 rps burst for short periods, otherwise best-effort is acceptable.
- Target uptime: 99.95% for the guaranteed lane.
- We expect steady baseline usage ~100 rps and occasional spikes. We want to understand:
  - pricing for guaranteed-lane retainer (monthly) + per-token (or per-request) uplift, and
  - committed spend discounts vs pure consumption pricing (what thresholds you recommend), and
  - whether you offer credits or pro-rated refunds for SLA misses.

Procurement also asked for a simple example invoice: committed spend X => discount Y, and how charges show up for burst usage that goes beyond the committed capacity.

Timeline: Gridly hopes to finalize commercial terms by the end of May if possible. Happy to set a quick call.

Thanks,
Danielle Harper
Director of Platform Partnerships
Gridly

From: Chloe Martin <chloe.martin@redwood.ai>
To: Danielle Harper <d.harper@gridly.com>
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>
Date: Sun, 17 May 2026 10:05:00 -0700
Subject: Re: SLA/packaging question — guaranteed lane during peaks

Hi Danielle — thanks for the clarity and timeline. Short answers up front and then a proposed next step:

- We can provide a guaranteed lane priced as a two-part solution: a monthly retainer for the dedicated slice (guaranteed capacity + prioritized routing) and a per-unit uplift for tokens/requests served from that lane.
- Committed spend discounts: typically 10–25% depending on term and volume. We’ll include a worked example for your baseline + spike profile.
- SLA credits: we support uptime credits on missed SLOs with a tiered credit schedule (we'll include the policy in the attachment).

I’ve attached an initial sketch of the SLA/price model (Gridly_SLA_proposal_v2.pdf) and a quick consumption-discount model (consumption_discount_model.xlsx). Can we schedule a 30–45m workshop this week to walk the Gridly platform and map the traffic profile to concrete pricing?

Proposed slots: Tue 05/19 10:00 PT, Wed 05/20 14:00 PT, Thu 05/21 09:30 PT. If procurement needs to join we'll include them.

Best,

Subject: Re: SLA/packaging question — guaranteed lane during peaks

Chloe — thanks, attaching our procurement constraints here (note: procurement@gridly.com is looped for visibility). A couple clarifications before the workshop:

- For bursts: is billing immediate for the uplift or do you bucket/average over the month? We want predictable invoicing.
- For committed discounts: are these applied to invoices monthly as a billing credit or as a reduced unit price? Procurement prefers a reduced unit price for simplicity.
- For guaranteed lane capacity: can you provide an option where we reserve a smaller dedicated window (e.g., 250 rps guaranteed + automatic short-term burst credit to 500 rps)? That would let us economize while still having headroom.

If you can sketch two quick scenarios in the workshop (conservative reserve vs aggressive reserve) that would help procurement decide on the commit level.

Best,
Danielle

Hi Danielle — thanks for the patience. Attached are two concrete scenarios and our recommended commercial approach:

Attachments: Gridly_SLA_proposal_v2.pdf, consumption_discount_model.xlsx

Summary (high level):
Scenario A — Conservative reserve (recommended for pilot)
- Reserve: 250 rps guaranteed lane (09:00–11:00 PT) + burst credits up to 500 rps for a total of 45 minutes/month free; additional burst billed at uplifted unit rate.
- Pricing: $6,500/month retainer for the reserved slice + reduced unit price applied to all usage once commit is in place (effective discount shown in spreadsheet).
- SLA credits: tiered credit schedule included. For pilot we propose 15% of monthly retainer for a P0 miss (trades predictability vs exposure).

Scenario B — Aggressive reserve (recommended for production)
- Reserve: 500 rps guaranteed lane (09:00–11:00 PT).
- Pricing: $11,000/month retainer + lower effective unit price; larger commitment band yields 18–22% discount tiers depending on term length.
- SLA credits: standard 25% retainer credit for P0 miss.

Billing mechanics (what we recommend):
- We recommend applying the committed discounts as a reduced unit price (simpler for procurement and invoicing). Retainer shows as a separate line item for reserved capacity. Bursts beyond reserved + credit window are billed at the uplifted unit price per the attached model.

Mutual action plan (proposed next steps):
1) Workshop: 45m session to walk the spreadsheet and map your traffic shape — Thu 05/27 10:00 PT or Fri 05/28 11:00 PT. Confirm which works.
2) Procurement: we'll provide redline-ready commercial terms (SOW + SLA appendix) within 2 business days after the workshop.
3) Pilot start: target week of 06/08 once contract is signed.

Please reply with which workshop slot works and whether procurement prefers scenario A or B as the starting point — we'll tailor the SOW precisely.

Thanks — looking forward to progressing.

Best,
